description: This topic explains the difference between active and passive voice, how to change sentences from one to the other, when the passive is preferred, the use of the agent with 'by', and keeping tenses consistent during the change.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence is written in the active voice?

options.text: The maize was harvested by the farmers.

mcq.explanation: In the active voice the subject performs the action. Here 'the farmers' do the harvesting, so the sentence is active.

mcq.questionText: What is the passive form of: 'The cook prepares the meal'?

options.text: The meal is prepared by the cook.
The meal was prepared by the cook.
The cook is prepared by the meal.

mcq.explanation: The simple present active becomes 'is/are + past participle' in the passive, keeping the same tense: 'is prepared'.

mcq.questionText: In a passive sentence, the word used to introduce the doer of the action is usually:
mcq.explanation: The agent (the doer of the action) in a passive sentence is normally introduced by the preposition 'by', as in 'painted by the artist'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence is in the passive voice?

options.text: The classroom was cleaned by the pupils.
The pupils clean the classroom daily.
The pupils are cleaning the classroom.

mcq.explanation: In the passive voice the subject receives the action. 'The classroom' receives the cleaning, and the doer follows 'by'.

mcq.questionText: Change to the passive: 'The teacher will mark the books.'

options.text: The books will mark the teacher.
The books are marked by the teacher.
The books will be marked by the teacher.
The books were marked by the teacher.

mcq.explanation: The future tense 'will mark' becomes 'will be marked' in the passive so that the tense stays the same.

mcq.questionText: Which is the correct passive form of: 'They are building a new bridge'?

options.text: A new bridge is being built.
A new bridge was being built.
A new bridge has been built.

mcq.explanation: The present continuous 'are building' becomes 'is/are being + past participle', giving 'is being built'.

mcq.questionText: Change to the active voice: 'The letter was written by Juma.'
mcq.explanation: The agent 'Juma' becomes the subject and the past passive 'was written' returns to the simple past active 'wrote'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence keeps the tense correct when changed to the passive of 'The dog has chased the cat'?

options.text: The cat is chased by the dog.
The cat was chased by the dog.
The cat has been chased by the dog.
The cat had been chased by the dog.

mcq.explanation: The present perfect 'has chased' becomes 'has been + past participle', so it is 'has been chased'.

mcq.questionText: When is the passive voice most suitable?

options.text: When the doer of the action is unknown or unimportant.
When we want to show who did the action clearly.
When writing a short text message to a friend.
When the subject is performing the action.

mcq.explanation: The passive is preferred when the doer is unknown, obvious or not important, so the focus stays on the action or the receiver.

mcq.questionText: Identify the agent in: 'The thief was arrested by the police.'
mcq.explanation: The agent is the doer of the action introduced by 'by'. Here 'the police' did the arresting.

mcq.questionText: Change to the passive: 'Someone has stolen my bicycle.'

options.text: My bicycle was stolen by someone.

mcq.explanation: The present perfect active 'has stolen' becomes 'has been stolen'. The vague agent 'someone' is usually dropped.

mcq.questionText: Which passive sentence is grammatically correct?

options.text: The song was sang by the choir.
The song was sung by the choir.
The song was sing by the choir.
The song is sang by the choir.

mcq.explanation: The passive needs the past participle, and the past participle of 'sing' is 'sung', not 'sang' or 'sing'.

mcq.questionText: Change to the active voice: 'Rice is grown by farmers in Mbeya.'

options.text: Farmers are growing rice in Mbeya.

mcq.explanation: The agent 'farmers' becomes the subject, and the present passive 'is grown' returns to the simple present active 'grow'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence cannot easily be changed into the passive voice?
mcq.explanation: Only sentences with a transitive verb (one that takes an object) can be made passive. 'Slept' has no object, so it cannot be changed.

mcq.questionText: Change to the passive (with the indirect object as subject): 'The headmaster gave the pupils prizes.'

options.text: The pupils were given prizes by the headmaster.
Prizes gave the pupils by the headmaster.
The pupils gave prizes by the headmaster.
The headmaster was given prizes by the pupils.

mcq.explanation: With two objects, the indirect object 'the pupils' can become the subject: 'The pupils were given prizes by the headmaster.'

fib.questionText: In the active voice, the _____ of the sentence performs the action.
fib.explanation: The subject is the doer of the action in an active sentence, such as 'The boy kicked the ball.'

fib.questionText: Passive form of 'Mary cleans the room': The room _____ cleaned by Mary.
fib.explanation: The simple present passive uses 'is/are + past participle'; with the singular 'room' we use 'is cleaned'.

fib.questionText: The doer of the action in a passive sentence is introduced by the preposition _____.
fib.explanation: The agent follows 'by', for example 'The wall was painted by the workers.'

fib.questionText: Change to passive: 'The dog bit the boy.' becomes 'The boy was _____ by the dog.'
fib.explanation: The passive needs the past participle of 'bite', which is 'bitten'.

fib.questionText: Passive of 'They will plant trees': Trees will _____ planted.
fib.explanation: The future passive is formed with 'will be + past participle', giving 'will be planted'.

fib.questionText: Active of 'The window was broken by Hamisi': Hamisi _____ the window.
fib.explanation: The agent becomes the subject and the past passive returns to the simple past active 'broke'.

fib.questionText: Passive of 'The pupils are doing the exercise': The exercise is _____ done by the pupils.
fib.explanation: The present continuous passive uses 'is/are being + past participle', giving 'is being done'.

fib.questionText: Only verbs that are _____ (those that take an object) can be changed into the passive voice.
fib.explanation: Transitive verbs have an object that can become the subject of the passive sentence.

fib.questionText: Passive of 'The chef has cooked the rice': The rice has _____ cooked by the chef.
fib.explanation: The present perfect passive uses 'has/have been + past participle', giving 'has been cooked'.

fib.questionText: When the doer of the action is unknown, the agent with 'by' is usually _____ from the passive sentence.
fib.explanation: If the doer is unknown or unimportant, the 'by + agent' phrase is left out, as in 'My phone was stolen.'

tf.questionText: In the active voice, the subject performs the action of the verb.
tf.explanation: Active voice means the subject is the doer, for example 'The girl wrote the letter.'

tf.questionText: In the passive voice, the subject receives the action instead of doing it.
tf.explanation: In the passive the subject is acted upon, as in 'The letter was written by the girl.'

tf.questionText: Every passive sentence must always include the agent with 'by'.
tf.explanation: The agent can be omitted when it is unknown, obvious or unimportant, for example 'The road was repaired.'

tf.questionText: The passive voice is formed using a form of the verb 'to be' plus the past participle.
tf.explanation: The passive is built as 'be (is/was/will be, etc.) + past participle', such as 'is closed' or 'was eaten'.

tf.questionText: Intransitive verbs such as 'sleep' and 'arrive' can be changed into the passive voice.
tf.explanation: Only transitive verbs (those with an object) can form the passive; intransitive verbs have no object to become the subject.

tf.questionText: When changing voice, the tense of the original sentence should be kept the same.
tf.explanation: Tense consistency is required; for example present 'eats' becomes 'is eaten', not 'was eaten'.

tf.questionText: The sentence 'The cake was eaten by the children' is in the passive voice.
tf.explanation: The subject 'the cake' receives the action and the doer 'the children' follows 'by', so it is passive.

tf.questionText: The passive voice is often used in scientific and formal reports.
tf.explanation: Formal and scientific writing often uses the passive to focus on the action rather than the doer, such as 'The water was heated.'

tf.questionText: Changing 'The boys play football' to the passive gives 'Football was played by the boys.'
tf.explanation: The original is present tense, so the correct passive is 'Football is played by the boys', not 'was played'.

tf.questionText: In the passive sentence, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject.
tf.explanation: When changing to passive, the active object moves to the front as the new subject, e.g. 'the ball' in 'The ball was kicked.'

summary.explanation: Example: 'The seeds were planted by the farmer.'

summary.correctAnswer: A form of 'to be' plus the past participle.
summary.explanation: For example 'is taken', 'was taken', 'will be taken'.

summary.questionText: The agent in a passive sentence
summary.explanation: Example: 'by the teacher' shows who performed the action.

summary.correctAnswer: When the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant.
summary.explanation: Example: 'The shop was robbed' when we do not know who did it.

summary.questionText: Verbs that can be made passive
summary.correctAnswer: Only transitive verbs that take an object.
summary.explanation: Intransitive verbs like 'sleep' cannot be made passive.

summary.correctAnswer: Keep the same tense when changing voice.

summary.questionText: When to use the passive voice
summary.correctAnswer: To focus on the action or receiver, or in formal writing.
summary.explanation: Common in reports and scientific writing.

summary.correctAnswer: Make the object the subject, use be + past participle, add 'by + doer'.
summary.explanation: 'Ali ate the fish' becomes 'The fish was eaten by Ali.'

summary.correctAnswer: Make the agent the subject and use the matching active verb.
summary.explanation: 'The fish was eaten by Ali' becomes 'Ali ate the fish.'

hoq.questionText: Which sentence shows the BEST reason for choosing the passive voice rather than the active?

options.text: 'My uncle drives a lorry.' to brag about my uncle.
'The records were destroyed during the fire.' because the doer is unknown and the loss is the focus.
'She loves mangoes.' to show her feelings clearly.
'We won the match.' to celebrate our team.

hoq.explanation: The passive is the better choice when the doer is unknown or unimportant and the focus is on what happened, which fits the destroyed records.

hoq.questionText: Change correctly to the passive, keeping the tense: 'The committee had approved the budget before the meeting ended.'

options.text: The budget was approved by the committee before the meeting ended.
The budget has been approved by the committee before the meeting ended.
The budget had been approved by the committee before the meeting ended.
The budget is approved by the committee before the meeting ended.

hoq.explanation: The past perfect 'had approved' becomes 'had been + past participle', giving 'had been approved' to keep the tense the same.

hoq.questionText: Which sentence has been changed from passive to active correctly without changing the meaning or tense?

options.text: Passive: 'The patients are being treated by the nurses.' Active: 'The nurses are treating the patients.'
Passive: 'The patients are being treated by the nurses.' Active: 'The nurses treated the patients.'
Passive: 'The patients are being treated by the nurses.' Active: 'The nurses will treat the patients.'
Passive: 'The patients are being treated by the nurses.' Active: 'The patients treat the nurses.'

hoq.explanation: The present continuous passive 'are being treated' becomes the present continuous active 'are treating', keeping the tense and meaning.
